function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

| **Banana** | What’s its approximate weight or length? A common reference is ~118 g (~5 inches). |
| **Quesadilla** | How many pieces did you eat, and do you know how much cheese/beans/meat it contained? If not, a rough estimate would help. |
| **Asparagus** | You said “four ounces”—is that cooked weight? |
| **Eggs** | Two whole eggs—do you remember if they were boiled, scrambled, fried, etc.? |
| **Gluten‑free Bread** | One slice—what brand/type so we can pull nutrition data? |

Also, it looks like there might be two separate breakfasts listed. Were all those items eaten together during the same morning session, or were they split across different times/days? Once we sort out the exact servings and timing, I’ll use the `log_food` function to record them properly.
